title: Roast marrow, squash and halloumi spelt bowls

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Squash, marrow, pearled spelt, halloumi, rocket, lemon and mint are all whole foods a grandparent could have had, with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including pearled spelt and halloumi, is an everyday line at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a saucepan and a sieve, with simple roasting and simmering.

works.reason: 250g spelt, 225g halloumi and two vegetables make a fair lunch for four, and the timings line up; a cook will naturally turn the marrow in the tray oil.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes of active work covers peeling and cubing the squash, seeding the marrow and slicing the halloumi, and the 30 minutes of cooking matches the two 15-minute roasts, with the spelt simmering alongside.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, each name matches its id, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm roast-veg grain bowl suits late September, and the marrow is a main component in the title rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholegrain spelt, two roast vegetables, halloumi and greens make a filling, balanced lunch a family would eat again.
